summary: Iteration 135 QA — War Room Live Chat, Scheduled Board Brief (cron), ServiceNow auto-ingest (cron), Per-obligation notify threshold. Verified: (a) POST /api/crisis/cases/{ref}/messages posts a chat msg and returns {message_id: MSG-####, text, author, role, created_at} with NO _id in payload; GET /api/crisis/cases/{ref}/messages returns list ascending by created_at with no _id leakage; empty text rejected (422); unauthenticated → 401. (b) PATCH /api/crisis/cases/{ref} with brief_schedule_hours=4 persists (verified by GET). (c) Cron: POST /api/cron/hourly-overdue-digest with correct WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET (64-char, read from /app/backend/.env whole value after first '=') → 200 {status:accepted}; 401 without/with wrong bearer. First cron after setting cadence writes a Communication event (source='Scheduled Brief', title contains 'Scheduled board brief emailed …') and sets brief_last_sent_at on the case; second immediate cron does NOT double-send (brief_last_sent_at unchanged, event count unchanged — cadence gate works). (d) Manual POST /api/crisis/ingest/servicenow still returns HTTP 400 with honest 'ServiceNow is not connected. Connect it in Connector Health…' when not connected. (e) Per-obligation notify threshold: POST creates obligation with notify_within_hours; PATCH accepts changes (24→6→72) and persists on GET; regulatory scan honours per-obligation threshold — obligation with deadline ~2h and threshold 1h did NOT set alert_state; raising threshold to 6h then re-scanning did set alert_state (regulatory scan gate honours notify_within_hours). (f) Regressions: /api/crisis/insight (grounded, 200 with headline/insights/actions), /api/connectors/health (200), /api/crisis/cases/{ref}/email-brief (200, sent>=1 via Resend). Frontend (Playwright, admin cookie session on /app/cyber-crisis-commander): after Demo Mode enabled — crisis-brief-cadence select present in header, default value=0, changing to 12 shows toast 'Auto-brief every 12h enabled.' and PATCHes case successfully. crisis-tab-warroom renders <WarRoomChat/> panel (crisis-war-room-chat) with crisis-chat-thread, crisis-chat-input, crisis-chat-send; posted 'TEST_iter135 UI chat msg' via Send → message rendered as crisis-chat-msg-* with author 'James Blan' + ADMIN badge + timestamp. crisis-tab-regulatory renders (obligation threshold selects present in code at line 943, testid=crisis-obligation-threshold-<id> — no obligations on currently-selected demo case CRISIS-0002 so no threshold selects rendered on that case; behaviour + PATCH verified via backend tests instead). No _id leakage observed anywhere in message payloads.

issues: Header row is very dense: Demo Mode + Ingest ServiceNow + Email Board Brief + Auto-brief select + Walkthrough + Refresh + Executive Brief all inline; on 1920px wraps ok but consider a small overflow menu on <1280px.

critical_code_review_comments: crisis_commander.py:post_message returns msg dict with 'created_at' as a string from _now() (good — no datetime serialisation issues) and copies dict before insert so ObjectId cannot leak into the response (msg.copy()); however the module also stores 'created_at' as string in Mongo, which means .sort('created_at', ASCENDING) is a string sort — fine while all writes use isoformat, but any future writer using a raw datetime would break ordering. Consider storing an additional numeric sort key or migrating to BSON datetimes.

crisis_commander.py:run_scheduled_briefs uses (now - last).total_seconds() < hours * 3600 — cadence gate is correct. However, the cursor iterates every non-Closed case globally every hour: for orgs with many active cases this could be I/O heavy. Add an index on {status:1, brief_schedule_hours:1} to short-circuit.

crisis_commander.py:run_scheduled_briefs — if send_email raises for one recipient, the loop swallows exceptions (silent 'except Exception: pass'). Consider logging via kernel logger so a broken Resend key isn't invisible in production. Also the audit event title says 'emailed to {len(emails)} recipient(s)' even if all sends failed silently.

crisis_commander.py:list_messages caps at .to_list(500). For long-running crises the War Room chat will silently truncate to first 500 messages ascending; consider pagination or reverse-cap 500 latest.

crisis_commander.py:CrisisMessage — max_length=2000 is fine but no rate limiting is applied; a runaway client could spam the endpoint. Consider a simple per-user, per-case rate-limit or Slowapi decorator.

scheduled.py:hourly_overdue_digest — three background tasks (regulatory + briefs + servicenow) added sequentially with add_task; FastAPI runs them in order in the same worker after response return — safe, but total wall time could exceed 1 minute for large tenants; consider fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task for parallelism if runtime becomes a concern.

success_rate.backend: 100% (14/14 tests pass — 5 initial failures under xdist were fixture races; serial run is clean)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (crisis-brief-cadence + PATCH toast, crisis-war-room-chat + thread + send verified; crisis-obligation-threshold-<id> present in JSX + backend PATCH verified)

rca of the issue: No bugs found. All four iter-135 features (War Room Live Chat, Scheduled Board Brief cron + cadence, ServiceNow auto-ingest no-op cron, Per-obligation notify threshold) behave per spec. The chat POST correctly strips _id via msg.copy() before insert, and GET projects {_id:0}. Scheduled brief cadence gate correctly prevents double-send (verified: two consecutive cron calls only produce one 'Scheduled Brief' Communication event and brief_last_sent_at is unchanged on the second call). ServiceNow manual endpoint returns honest 400 with expected 'not connected' detail. Regulatory scan alert_state field correctly honours per-obligation notify_within_hours.
